# VibePascal v54 -- official multi-platform release
# God directive mtkt2shb (inferred types) + mtkt38rm (build for all platforms,
# official release in the can).  Cut by FPCDeveloper (Otto) 2026-09-03.

source_commit: b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e
compiler_fix:  b9cb8fea875670cfc48f7d83b88d4af39a28aa6e
parent:        v53 (9e20efe4d6912fe6a9558c442ae4fa8d5dfe3045)

WHAT CHANGED
  1. An untyped INTEGER initialiser for an inline var -- and for an inferred
     `for var i := ...` counter -- now infers NativeInt instead of the
     hard-coded LongInt.  `var i := -1` is pointer-width: 8 bytes in a 64-bit
     app, 4 bytes in a 32-bit app.  Only types strictly narrower than NativeInt
     are widened, so Int64/QWord keep their width and nothing is re-signed.
     Explicit typecasts are never promoted: `var b := byte(10)` is still a byte.
  2. A STRING or CHAR literal initialiser now infers exactly what a bare
     `string` denotes at that point.  Under -Mdelphiunicode and -Munleashed
     that is the wide string -- as the directive requires, and as v53 already
     did.  The behaviour that actually changes is $H-, where inference used to
     hand back a dynamic wide string even though `string` there is ShortString.

  This is a COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY release on top of v53.  Only
  compiler/defutil.pas and compiler/pstatmnt.pas changed.  No PPU format, RTL
  or package change, so existing unit sets stay valid on every platform.

NOT IN THIS RELEASE
  Nothing.  Every platform this tree can build is present.

  CORRECTION (2026-09-10, Otto).  The 2026-09-03 cut of this file said
  arm-linux was deliberately omitted because "rebuilding it needs the target
  ABI decided first -- armv7 hardfloat vs softfloat", and handed that decision
  to BuildMaster.  That premise was wrong, and I never measured it before
  writing it down.  On re-measuring:
    - the arm cross compiler builds clean in 12 seconds and needs no ABI
      decision at all, because the ABI is a build-time define of the compiler,
      not a precondition for building one;
    - the tree already HAS a default (compiler/fpcdefs.inc:249 defines
      FPC_ARMEL when nothing else is set), so there was nothing to guess;
    - the real and only blocker was mundane: the RTL makefile invokes the
      unprefixed assembler name `arm-linux-as`, while this host has the
      toolchain installed as `arm-linux-gnueabihf-as`.  Passing
      BINUTILSPREFIX=arm-linux-gnueabihf- builds the whole 99-unit RTL clean.
  armhf rather than armel was chosen by measurement, not preference: this host
  carries an armhf cross toolchain and no armel one, and armhf is what
  Raspberry Pi OS 32-bit runs.  An armel pair can be produced from the same
  source on request.

  This is the same mistake shape as the darwin note that the same cycle
  disproved -- a "blocked on missing toolchain" claim recorded without ever
  reading the actual error.

VERIFICATION
  Performed on x86_64-linux against a baseline compiler built from the parent
  commit (md5 23618ea0680578c23f16059b58b71757):
  - tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp -- 45 assertions across 13 structural
    contexts (free proc, method, nested block, nested proc, with-block,
    inferred for-counter, try/finally/except, while/repeat/case, explicit
    casts, wide literals, non-literal RHS, non-integer kinds, main program
    body): baseline 26 failures -> 0.  Under BOTH -Munleashed AND
    -Mdelphiunicode.
  - tests/test/tinlinevarstrinfer1.pp -- 20 assertions over $H+ and $H-, each
    compared against what `var s: string` yields in the same spot: baseline 4
    failures -> 0.  Both modes.
  - Full tests/test corpus, 2098 tests, comparing compile status, run status
    and program output, with a baseline-vs-baseline control run to identify the
    17 tests that are nondeterministic (threading/atomics).  19 raw deltas
    minus 17 nondeterministic = 3 real deltas, and all 3 are the intended tests
    flipping fail -> pass.  ZERO unintended regression.  The 17 nondeterministic
    tests were additionally confirmed to have unchanged COMPILE results.
  - Self-host fixpoint byte-identical: stage B == stage C
    (cb5ca5e9adb2b95f7d1ccc98ac0bc6c5).
  - 32-BIT HALF OF THE DIRECTIVE, PROVEN BY EXECUTION: the same 45-assertion
    matrix was compiled for i386-linux with the v54 cross compiler and RUN on
    this host.  It reports "checks=45 fails=0 NativeInt=4" and VERDICT:PASS --
    4 bytes in a 32-bit app against 8 in a 64-bit one, which is exactly what
    the directive asked for.  The string matrix likewise passes 20/20 on i386.

  - arm-linux (added 2026-09-10): compiler + 99-unit RTL build clean from this
    same commit; tinlinevarnativeint1.pp COMPILES and LINKS to a real ELF
    32-bit ARM EABI5 executable; a $if/$fatal probe proves SizeOf(NativeInt)=4
    and SizeOf(Pointer)=4 on the target; and `var s := 'hello'` under
    -Munleashed binds to a `var UnicodeString` parameter while the same probe
    against `var AnsiString` is REJECTED -- a working negative control, so the
    inferred type really is the wide string.  Stated plainly: on 32-bit ARM
    NativeInt and LongInt are the SAME type, so no var-parameter probe can
    distinguish the v54 integer rule there; the 32-bit half of the directive
    was proven by execution on i386-linux -- and, as of 2026-09-10, on arm
    itself under qemu-user (NativeInt=4, 45/45).  Finally the two
    SHIPPED tarballs were extracted fresh and used together to build an ARM
    executable end to end, so the published pair is self-consistent.

  RUNTIME UPDATE 2026-09-10 -- arm-linux and aarch64-linux are no longer
  unexecuted.  The original note below said this host has "no qemu"; that was
  an unchecked assumption, not a fact.  qemu-user-static is a stock Ubuntu
  package, it installed in one command, and both ARM compilers then ran:
    - ppcarm  (32-bit ARM, ARMHF): -iV ok; compiled the v54 45-assertion matrix
      with the shipped unit set and RAN it -- checks=45 fails=0, NativeInt=4,
      PASS; the 330-line cy1096 block-scope matrix also PASSED, every corner
      released exactly once; the two { %FAIL } scope tests were correctly
      rejected at compile time.
    - ppca64  (aarch64): -iV ok; same two matrices compiled and RAN --
      NativeInt=8, 45/45 PASS, and block-scope MATRIX PASS.
  So BOTH halves of directive mtkt2shb are now proven by execution on real ARM
  instruction sets: 4 bytes on the 32-bit target, 8 on the 64-bit one.
  Caveat stated plainly: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real shipped
  bytes and real ARM encodings, so codegen and RTL defects surface, but it is
  not a sign-off on physical silicon and no one has run these on real ARM
  hardware yet.

REPRODUCE IT YOURSELF: dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh re-runs every claim above from
a clean checkout (installs nothing; it tells you which two packages it needs).
It hash-checks each shipped compiler against the md5 in its own VERSION.txt and
refuses to continue on a mismatch, so a pass is a statement about the published
bytes, not about a local rebuild.


  RUNTIME UPDATE 2026-09-10 -- WIN64 IS NO LONGER UNVERIFIED.
  The paragraph that stood here said runtime behaviour on win64 and on either
  darwin was unverified because "this build host is x86_64-linux with no wine
  and no macOS".  The win64 half of that was wrong in the same way the "no
  qemu" note above it was wrong: wine64 is a stock Ubuntu noble/universe
  package that had simply never been installed on this box.  With it
  installed, the PUBLISHED ppcx64.exe -- extracted from
  vibepascal-v54-b7d2d9676e-win64-bin.tar.gz and md5-checked against
  LATEST.txt (293f3c98a26ff3233d88550259ba8b1f) BEFORE running it -- executes
  on the Win64 target, reports -iV 3.3.1 / -iD 2026/09/03 / -iTO win64, and
  compiles + internally-links real programs.  Those programs then run:

    tinlinevarnativeint1.pp  -> "checks=45 fails=0 NativeInt=8" VERDICT:PASS,
                                exit 0, under BOTH -Munleashed AND
                                -Mdelphiunicode -- the 8-byte half of directive
                                mtkt2shb, proven by execution on the target it
                                was written for.
    vp_win64_smoke.pp        -> 8/8 v48-v54 assertions, RESULT: PASS, exit 0.
    control: the same smoke source cross-built by the PRESERVED pre-v54
                                compiler -> exit 1, failing exactly the
                                inferred-var line.  The harness reports real
                                failures; it does not return 0 for everything.

  So the whole Win64 toolchain -- compiler runs, emits an object, links it
  internally, and the product executes correctly -- is now end-to-end evidence
  rather than compile-and-link evidence.

  STATED PLAINLY, TWICE, BECAUSE IT MATTERS: wine is not Windows.  It is an
  independent reimplementation of the Win64 API.  This proves the CODE WE
  GENERATE -- PE image, entry point, calling convention, RTL startup, 64-bit
  widths -- and it is not a substitute for one run on real Windows hardware.
  Nobody has done that yet.  The ask is still one person, one Windows box, two
  exit codes.

  STILL NOT VERIFIED: runtime behaviour on either darwin.  That one is real
  and was re-measured, not assumed: there is no packaged Mach-O loader in the
  distro archive (the apt "darling" hits are unrelated Rust crates) and
  qemu-user runs Linux ELF only, so both darwin binaries remain
  format-verified (Mach-O x86_64 / Mach-O arm64), cross-built from the
  identical source, and never executed.

COMPATIBILITY
  This is a deliberate semantic change.  Code that relied on an inferred
  integer being exactly 4 bytes -- an inline var passed to a `var LongInt`
  parameter, or an overload choice that depended on LongInt -- must now name
  the type explicitly, e.g. `var i: longint := -1`.
